test_case.agent_script:
=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are asking about Child Benefit for 1 child:
  - Alex is 16 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 16, has left education or training and been registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services for less than 20 weeks
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

circumstances: Child is 16, has left education or training and been registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services for less than 20 weeks

Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation

Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To start, I need to know about your child. **How old is your child?**

This is important because:
- **Under 16**: Children automatically qualify (with some conditions)
- **16-19**: They may qualify if they're in approved education or training
- **20 or over**: Generally not eligible for Child Benefit

Please tell me your child's age so we can continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. My child is 16 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you! Since your child is 16 years old, they fall into the 16-19 age category. This means they may still qualify for Child Benefit if they meet certain education or training requirements.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to understand your child's education or training situation. For 16-19 year olds, there are specific requirements.

**Which of the following applies to your child?**

1. **Currently in approved education or training** - They are enrolled in and attending an approved course or training program

2. **Recently left education** - They've left education or training within the last 20 weeks

3. **Neither** - They're not in education/training and haven't recently left

Please let me know which situation applies to your 16-year-old child.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: They recently left education. They've signed up with the careers service to get some help figuring out what to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. Since your child recently left education, they may still be eligible for Child Benefit during an extension period. Let me check the specific requirements for this.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news - registering with the careers service is one of the qualifying services! Now I need to check a couple of specific things:

**1. How long ago did your child leave education?** (I need to know if it's within the last 20 weeks)

**2. Is your child 16 or 17 years old?** (You mentioned they're 16, but I want to confirm they haven't turned 18 yet)

This matters because there's a special 20-week extension period for children aged 16-17 who have:
- Left approved education or training
- Registered with a government careers service (which your child has done), Connexions, or the armed services

The extension lasts for up to 20 weeks OR until they turn 18, whichever comes first.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, they're still 16 - haven't turned 17 yet. They left school just a few weeks ago, so definitely within the 20 weeks.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Since your child:
- Is 16 years old (hasn't turned 18)
- Left education just a few weeks ago (within the 20-week period)
- Has registered with the careers service (a qualifying service)

They meet the extension eligibility requirements. Now let me check the next requirement.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check their work status.

**Is your child working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work at all)?**

This is important because children aged 16 or over who work 24 hours or more per week (and aren't in approved education/training) don't qualify for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, they're not working at all right now. They're just focusing on figuring out their next steps with the careers service.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Since your child is not working at all, they meet this requirement. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check about benefits:

**Is your child receiving any benefits in their own right**, such as:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

If they are NOT receiving these types of benefits in their own right, answer "No, they're not receiving these benefits."

If they ARE receiving these benefits in their own right, answer "Yes, they are receiving benefits."

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, they're not receiving any benefits in their own right.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check about apprenticeships:

**Is your child in an apprenticeship?**

This matters because different types of apprenticeships have different rules:
- **England**: All apprenticeships disqualify from Child Benefit
- **Scotland**: Modern Apprenticeships disqualify
- **Wales**: Foundation Apprenticeships are approved (don't disqualify), but other apprenticeships do disqualify

If your child is not in any apprenticeship at all, that's fine. Please let me know their apprenticeship status.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, they're not in an apprenticeship. Like I said, they just left school and are working with the careers service to figure out what they want to do.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for confirming! Since your child is not in an apprenticeship, they meet this requirement. Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency status, as this is a key requirement for Child Benefit.

**Do you meet any of the following residency requirements?**

1. **Normally live in the UK** - You're ordinarily resident in the UK

2. **Crown servant living abroad** - You're living abroad as a Crown servant or in certain qualifying countries

3. **EU Settlement Scheme status** - You have settled or pre-settled status (with additional conditions for pre-settled)

Which of these applies to you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm normally resident here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Since you normally live in the UK, you meet the residency requirement. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check if you're responsible for the child. **Are you responsible for your child?** This means you meet at least one of these:

1. **You live with the child** - The child lives in your household

2. **You contribute to their upkeep** - You pay at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount towards their care (food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents, etc.)

3. **You pay maintenance** - You make maintenance payments under a court order or agreement that equals or exceeds the Child Benefit amount

Do any of these apply to you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, they live with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Since your child lives with you, you meet the responsibility requirement. Let me continue.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check about other potential claimants:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for this child?**

For example:
- The child's other parent
- Another family member
- Anyone else

If someone else is claiming but you've both agreed that you should claim instead, please let me know that too.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Since no one else is claiming, let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to understand your child's living situation:

**Which of the following applies to your child?**

1. **In hospital** - Currently staying in a hospital
2. **In care** - In local authority care
3. **Fostered** - Living with foster carers
4. **Normal living** - Living at home with you (none of the above apply)

Which situation applies to your 16-year-old?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Normal living - they're just living at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Just one final check:

**Is the local council paying towards your child's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, is the council providing financial support for where your child lives or their day-to-day care costs?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything towards their accommodation or maintenance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! Let me move to the final outcome.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
🎉 **Great news! You ARE eligible for Child Benefit!**

Based on the assessment, you meet all the eligibility requirements:

✅ Your child is 16 years old  
✅ They recently left education (within the 20-week extension period)  
✅ They're registered with the careers service  
✅ They're not working 24+ hours per week  
✅ They're not receiving benefits in their own right  
✅ They're not in a disqualifying apprenticeship  
✅ You normally live in the UK  
✅ Your child lives with you  
✅ No one else is claiming for this child  
✅ The council is not paying for their accommodation or maintenance

**Next Steps:**

1. **Apply** - You can apply online or by post using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** - For yourself and your child
3. **Provide documentation** - Your child's birth certificate or adoption certificate
4. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge** - If you or your partner earns over £60,000, you may need to pay some or all of it back through tax
5. **Payments** - Child Benefit is typically paid every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

**Important reminder**: The 20-week extension will last until either 20 weeks after your child left education OR until they turn 18, whichever comes first. If your child starts approved education/training during this time, they may continue to qualify under different rules.

For more information and to apply, visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Do you have any questions about the eligibility or the application process?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's brilliant, thank you so much for going through all of that with me! That's really helpful to know that they're still eligible even though they've left school. I don't have any other questions right now - I'll get started on the application. Thanks again!

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome! I'm so glad I could help clarify that for you. Yes, that 20-week extension period is really helpful for young people who've just left education and are working out their next steps - it's great that your child is already engaged with the careers service.

Before you go, I need to formally record the outcome of our assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Good luck with your application, and if you have any questions in the future, feel free to come back. Take care! 😊
